questions.q: The main indicator of lithium battery wear?
options: The cycle count written on the sticker
The color of the wrap after a flight
The battery's mass on the scales
The internal resistance of the cells
questions.explain: Growing IR — less output under load and more heating; it is measured with the same instrument at the same temperature.
Storage 3.80–3.90 V; they are not kept full for longer than a day.

questions.q: A prop touched the grass on landing, no visible cracks. What do you do?
options: Keep flying, since there are no cracks
questions.explain: A prop is replaced after a strike: microcracks are invisible, and failure in flight means losing the aircraft.

questions.q: A motor's MTBF is 1000 h. The probability of running 1000 h without failure?
Motor reliability is r. The reliability of a quadcopter in terms of motors?
questions.explain: A series system: all four are needed, R = r⁴.

questions.q: Why doesn't a hexa always survive a motor failure?
options: Six motors are heavier than four
A motor failure is not dangerous for a hexa at all
It depends on the frame, thrust and firmware
questions.explain: The ability to fly home on five motors is tested, not assumed.

questions.q: Vibration grows from flight to flight with the same props. The likely cause?
options: Wear of the bearings or mounting
Cold weather on the day of the flight
questions.explain: A vibration trend is an early sign of bearing wear and loosened mounting.

questions.q: What does the “bathtub” curve give you for operations?
options: A reason not to replace components until the first failure
Acceptance testing of new units and replacement by service life
questions.explain: Early failures are caught by acceptance testing, wear-out by replacement before its zone.
